q: According to Newton's second law, an object that is accelerating must have a _____ acting on it.
e: According to Newton's second law, an object that is accelerating must have a net force acting on it. Net force is the vector sum; zero net force means constant velocity. centrifugal force or fictitious force is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An object moving in a circle must have a force applied to it to keep it moving in the circle, and this force is known as the _____.
e: An object moving in a circle must have a force applied to it to keep it moving in the circle, and this force is known as the centripetal force. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle. centrifugal force or normal force is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal acceleration which is directed towards the _____ of the circle at any moment.
e: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal acceleration which is directed towards the centre of the circle at any moment. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point. edge or tangent is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the absence of centripetal force, the object would not move along a circle but move in a _____, according to Newton's first law.
e: In the absence of centripetal force, the object would not move along a circle but move in a straight line, according to Newton's first law. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r. circular path or curved path is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When whirling a body attached to a string, the _____ force behaves as a centripetal force.
e: When whirling a body attached to a string, the tension force behaves as a centripetal force. String tension can be the inward centripetal force on a whirling ball. frictional or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An attractive force exists between the sun and the earth in a direction _____ to the path of the earth.
e: An attractive force exists between the sun and the earth in a direction perpendicular to the path of the earth. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles. parallel or tangent is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The _____ attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force.
e: The Coulomb attractive force between the nucleus and the electron acts as the required centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r. Gravitational or Magnetic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When a car turns in a circular path, the _____ force acts normally to the direction of motion of the car.
e: When a car turns in a circular path, the frictional force acts normally to the direction of motion of the car. On a level curve, frictional force of the tires supplies F_c. normal or tension is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When a car moves in a circular path which is inclined to the horizontal, the _____ component of normal force is the required centripetal force.
e: When a car moves in a circular path which is inclined to the horizontal, the vertical component of normal force is the required centripetal force. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r. horizontal or diagonal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The upward thrust (lifting force) acts normally to an aeroplane body; when it tilts, the horizontal component provides the _____ force.
e: The upward thrust (lifting force) acts normally to an aeroplane body; when it tilts, the horizontal component provides the centripetal force. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle. centrifugal or frictional is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: On a flat road (unbanked road), the centripetal force is supplied by _____ between the tires and the road.
e: On a flat road (unbanked road), the centripetal force is supplied by friction between the tires and the road. Centripetal force is the real net inward force that keeps an object on a circular path, F_c = mv²/r. tension or gravity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: If the frictional force is not sufficient, such as under wet and slippery conditions, the car will _____ out of the circular path.
e: If the frictional force is not sufficient, such as under wet and slippery conditions, the car will skid out of the circular path. If friction cannot supply mv²/r, the car will skid out of the curve. accelerate or stop is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Banking of roads is raising the _____ edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge.
e: Banking of roads is raising the outer edge of the curved road higher than the inner edge. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement. inner or horizontal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The angle that the inclined track makes with horizontal is called the angle of _____.
e: The angle that the inclined track makes with horizontal is called the angle of banking. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement. friction or tension is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: For every banked curve, there is a limiting speed at which the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the _____ force.
e: For every banked curve, there is a limiting speed at which the entire centripetal force is supplied by the horizontal component of the frictional force. On a level curve, frictional force of the tires supplies F_c. normal or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the _____ force between the tires and the road is not required.
e: At the limiting speed on a banked curve, the centrifugal force between the tires and the road is not required. Centrifugal names the apparent outward effect in the rotating frame. frictional or normal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Since there is no vertical motion on a banked road, the net force on the car in the y direction is _____.
e: Since there is no vertical motion on a banked road, the net force on the car in the y direction is maximum. A banked track tilts so the horizontal part of the normal force can supply some or all of the centripetal requirement. zero or equal to gravity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
